notes: Rule edit; derivability unlikely (stated, but less often than the other rules). R1 considered: Wikipedia adds 'so long as they meet qualifications such as age and citizenship', every life peer created does; serving Supreme Court justices are barred while in office and, since 2014, peers may retire, which ends a seat already held but not the entitlement creation gives. Thatcher and Olivier died before 2014 and never retired; neither was ever disqualified. Olivier was never an MP, so 'Commons' for him comes only from the rule. Thatcher sat in the Commons until 1992, so the question is limited to 1992 onwards. New members are fictional. 'One house at a time' is now a bridge with a check on the two well-known members' questions: 'which house' and the clash in the by-name worlds need it (formal check, FINDINGS B3).
